Quick and easy to prepare, the only way to mess this up is not pay attention to the cooking time.

2-3 cups of flour
2 teaspoons of baking powder
1 cup of sugar
1 cup of shortening/butter
a pinch of salt
vanilla
3 eggs

aluminium foil
2 cookie sheets
a good cookie-lifting spatula

Before we jump in, remember that substitution-jutsu works here. You can swap half the sugar for an alternative, like honey or molasses. You can also throw in things like raisins or chocolate chips if that interests you. Using three tablespoons of cocoa powder adds a chocolate hint to the cookies, without going crazy.

In a large bowl beat the eggs lightly to break the yolks as one would for scrambled eggs, then mix in the shortening. Soften the butter before hand if you must by heating it a little.

When the shortening/egg mixture is loose, add the vanilla and then the sweetening agent, mix well then add the salt to the liquid mixture.

Add the baking powder then slowly add the flour as needed to reach a proper doughy state, you may not need all three cups of flour, or may even need a little more based on your eggs and how closely you measured. You will be fine as long as you get it to a dough state and not a batter state.

This is because you then grab it by your spoons and make balls that you put onto a foiled cookie sheet that you have lightly greased, be it with PAM or butter, or whateer. The pan then goes into an oven heated to 350°F and the cookies bake for between 15-20 minutes. Turn them around inside the oven at the 7 minute mark to make sure one set of cookies doesn't get too much heat. At the 12 minute mark you need to start watching them, because some people's ovens are a little hotter than others.

Pull them out when they are turning brown and you are golden. They take about 15 minutes to become solid enough to take off the foil without them falling apart.

The recipe itself has been bouncing around my grandmother's family for longer than any of them know. But for my great-grandmother, it was called, "grannie Gilbert's sugar cookies." So, it is kinda a traditional one.
